title: I need help
author: What_four
selftext:
in my game I have a top-down 2d hexagonal map. the map is supposed to wrap around on itself so if the player or enemy crosses the border of one side of the map they are simultaneously entering through the opposite side of the hexagon map. imagine the map appearing as periodic tiling. whenever you see the border of the map you can see what's across it as soon as it is in view. enemies should be able to cross the border.

i feel like i'm bad at explaining this. i'm trying to explain to ai in the summer engine but it's been very frustrating. does anyone know a good way to explain this to ai?

comments.author: Blake9712
comments.body: The map loops around itself so when the player crosses over onto the right side the left side reloads but the left side needs to reload before the right side is visible and it should likely load assets in stages so as to not cause stuttering?

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
I copy-paste your post as prompt and here is what I got from AI. maybe you just need a stronger AI model.

\------

I actually think the Reddit user explained the concept pretty well. I immediately understood what they're trying to accomplish.

What they're describing is a seamless, wraparound hexagonal world with periodic boundary conditions. The tricky part isn't explaining the concept; it's implementing it correctly.

There are three separate problems:

1. World wrapping: When a player crosses one edge of the hexagon, they reappear at the corresponding position on the opposite edge, preserving their direction and velocity.
2. Seamless rendering: The camera must display the adjacent copy of the world beyond each boundary. Otherwise, objects will suddenly pop into view when crossing an edge.
3. Gameplay continuity: Enemies, projectiles, AI pathfinding, collision detection, and distance calculations must all respect the wrapping. An enemy immediately across a boundary should be considered nearby, not on the opposite side of the map.
